reason: While the text demonstrates Yahweh's all-powerful nature through miracles (the burning bush, Moses' leprous hand, the Nile turning to blood), it contradicts the characterization of God as 'remote.' This passage (Exodus 3-4) is fundamentally about intimate divine engagement: God appears directly to Moses, speaks with him face-to-face, describes His own awareness and concern for His people's suffering ('I have surely seen the affliction of My people...and have heard their cry'), declares 'I have come down to deliver them,' and engages in direct dialogue addressing Moses' objections. God is depicted as personally present, relationally engaged, and responsively involved—the antithesis of remote.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
